source.title: Universal statistics of Fisher information in deep neural networks: mean field approach
source.authors: Ryo Karakida; S. Akaho; S. Amari

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training-loss outcomes across learning rates and checks them against a theoretically estimated convergence threshold, using SGD on CIFAR-10. It does not measure the specific sharpness dynamics or above-initial-stability recovery described in V5.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 loss map and the text describing its agreement with the learning-rate estimate are relevant. The reported results are training losses, not training classification errors. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses prior mean-field signal-propagation results and recommended initialization settings to derive and evaluate FIM-based learning-rate estimates. Its results do not test any listed version. In particular, its convergence threshold concerns curvature at an assumed zero-loss minimum, rather than the initial linearized-model stability limit or evolving sharpness specified in V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the learning-rate application but omits the main contribution: asymptotic FIM eigenvalue statistics imply many locally flat directions and a few strongly distorted directions. The authors report agreement with numerical experiments and suggest applications to Fisher-Rao norms and learning-rate selection, while acknowledging assumptions and the need to establish broader applicability.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes FIM statistics in randomly connected fully connected networks and examines learning-rate behavior; it does not use the training recipes or measures in the claim's cited studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Training losses vary with learning rate and network activation; the paper reports CIFAR-10 results as almost the same as MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: For four-layer fully connected tanh, ReLU, and linear teacher-student networks trained with squared loss and momentum 0.9 for 100 steps, the authors report exploding loss above their estimated critical learning rate. Some exploding runs also occur below it, with that region shrinking as width increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An FIM-based local convergence threshold at an assumed randomly generated zero-loss minimum estimates learning-rate boundaries in these teacher-student experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: One-epoch SGD experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 reportedly agree with the FIM-based learning-rate estimate, despite the theorem's assumptions not generally holding for these benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FIM statistics can approximately predict learning rates associated with exploding training loss in these fully connected benchmark networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2019; PMLR Volume 89)
record.problems: CIFAR-10 training-loss results are presented as color maps without extractable numeric values. Training ran for one epoch with mini-batches of 500; the text says the global-minimum conditions of the theorem do not generally hold for these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the only relevant CIFAR-10 results are figure-only loss maps, and the text provides no exact values for individual activation and learning-rate conditions. The study does not report the specific V5 dynamics required for a row linked to that version.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including label corruption and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special plain-network initializations, or Fixup.
Comparative effects of initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.

Recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, transient loss and curvature dynamics, sustained edge-of-stability training, and divergence relative to a measured initial stability threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V5 tested_not_extracted designation to not tested. Loss maps alone do not establish the particular stability dynamics V5 names. The absence of exact figure values is therefore not the reason to withhold V5 verdicts. No result rows were supplied, and no missing result bearing on a listed version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, zero or near-zero error, CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model-size effects, and early stopping are not tested.

The paper tests learning-rate-dependent training loss and divergence on CIFAR-10, but does not report sharpness dynamics or a brief loss rise followed by recovery above the initial linearized model's stability limit. Figure 2 gives loss maps without extractable numeric values; the text says CIFAR-10 results were almost the same as MNIST and refers to Figure C.2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
